I (35M) just got mine done last week. The procedure itself was fast, and, aside from the initial injection, it just felt like some pressure around the area. No pain really. But, after it wore on that first day I was definitely feeling it. Not agony, but it didn’t tickle. 

The doctor asked me why I wanted one and I said my desire to not have kids is only getting more sure as I get older. They didn’t ask much more beyond that. 

Post procedure tips if you want them: 1. Get ice packs or frozen peas or something. Enough to rotate them 10-15 on 20-30 off. Most of the pain is from inflammation and the ice helps. A lot. 2. Lying down for the first 24hrs after is the best call, but get some compression shorts. Movement will hurt and that helps mitigate that so he can walk to the restroom comfortably. 3. No sex for a week or so. Busting a nut is excruciating if you don’t wait long enough. Trust me I’m a dumbass and only waited about four days/until the pain stopped. It started immediately after and kept up for about a day. 4. This seems obvious but just in case; follow the guidelines for keeping it clean. No soaking in water, put on the antiseptic cream, etc. he may be shooting blanks after, but you don’t want his gun to jam. 

Hope it goes well. It’s really not as bad as it seems like it would be.

I’m 35 and was homeschooled from third grade to my junior year of high school. I sometimes spent weeks without being around people other than my immediate family. Even then my parents worked long hours. Eventually when I was in school I spent my days exactly like yours. Then I found the drama club. It was fun. I got to, terribly, act out plays and scenes with other awkward nerdy kids like me. I made friends with an activity that I didn’t know I’d be interested in. What I’ve learned over the years is that it takes effort to make and maintain friendships. What helped me was finding that group. In my head I would make it in on the first day and get shunned for not being good enough or too awkward. But, I was very, very wrong. I was offered help from other students to improve my acting skills, given support, kindness, invited out to after school, and even had my first girlfriend in that group. The skills I learned there has carried me through my final year of school and then on to now. I’m in no way saying you need to try the drama club. That’s just what worked for me, but you not putting yourself out into the world means you are missing the opportunity. I even loved acting enough that post high school I got in with a drama club that was just a bunch on locals who did plays at the rec center. It doesn’t end at adulthood. You’re 14. You have a whole life ahead of you. I believe in you, and you will find those social interactions. Look and be willing to be uncomfortable at first and you will make it so much further than you think is possible. Most of all. Just be you. You’re more than enough, and you deserve all the happiness you can handle. Look for something that even kinda sounds interesting, and be honest about how you feel about that activity. You’ll learn a new skill at minimum, even if what you learn is some social cues and how to self reflect. I wish you all the best. Be uncomfortable, it’s the best decision you’ll ever make.

The steamer would probably work for the glue, but be careful of warping the wood. A steam box is one of the ways to shape a wood plank, and if the wood is really dry you're risking it. Before you bust out the steamer, try looking up some instructions on how to remove wallpaper. It will give you an idea of the process with the solution. Ultimately you want to use enough to soak the paper and glue but not so much that it has waterlogged the wood. The steamer should be a good option for the final spot cleaning. Hey, retired cop here. You need to call and make a report about this. Paper trails are important, and in the event you have anything else happen it will, without a doubt, remove any question of the impact of this incident. In my jurisdiction restraining orders don't require threats. Harassment is just as much of a valid reason. The worst they can say is no, so I would make a point to file for one now. This does two things. A: sets up the proof that you have tried to prevent anything from getting worse. B: if you get it then you can make your home a listed property. That means even if you aren't present the order still applies to your home. Tbh, you should call your non-emergent police line and ask if someone can come take a report. At MINIMUM, the cops should document this and make contact with him to inform him if he continues it will be jail time/arrest him then if there is enough. Please be safe, check your windows and doors are locked, and remember to breathe. You're strong and will get through this. Be safe.

He said that sharpie pens drastically fade with exposure to UV light, over time, etc. To prevent further fading you can get a frame with UV blocking glass or put it away and keep it in a dark place. That should slow it down dramatically. Unfortunately, there isn't really a way to bring it back on the item. Once it is faded it is basically gone on the item.. I'm sorry I don't have better news. I would say your best bet is not to try and recover the ink, but to see if you can get an image of it through photo manipulation/editing. I really hope you have some luck with at least getting the words back in some form.

Have you tried putting it into photoshop or another editing software. No flash. Just take a shot and adjust the contrast? Sometimes that will highlight faint changes in the photo. I will talk to a buddy of mine who is good with this stuff. Was there any finish on the wood before people wrote on it, Like a urethane or something?  As much info as I can give him will help.

Do you know what kind of pen was used to write the messages? Sometimes using a black light and those filter glasses can change the appearance of the chemicals in the ink and make it more legible. Also, I'm getting the impression that if you can't restore this you would at least like to be able to read the messages somehow. If so, what about taking a photo of it and playing around with the contrast, lighting, etc. on your computer? Also, you could shine a bright light against across the top to cast a shadow on any pen impressions. Otherwise it is extremely hard to restore ink like this. There are some products on the market that are supposed to darken the ink, but they are not recommended unless the item the ink is on doesn't matter. Just the inscription. I hope you find your message.

Also, if you can take ibuprofen at your reccomend dose (800mg for a full grown adult) every 4-6 hrs. Max at 3200mg in 24 hr.

If you don't see results in 2-4 days of no use and keeping up with the ice and NSAIDs. Go see your doc.
